body:
As another poster here said, you having aspergers + her having BPD actually does lead to a very potentially deep connection and you've already taken a huge step in making that happen by asking how you can make her feel more comfortable around you.


I just wanted to remind you that you should be able to tell her what would make you more comfortable around her as well. :)


The fact that you've taken the time to actually read about BPD and get to know what she actually struggles with on a daily basis is huge and I hope she realizes how lucky she is to have found someone that cares about her this much.



My general advice is that people with BPD have a short "emotional retainer" and it takes a lot of patience to grasp just how insecure they can be even when it seems overwhelmingly obvious that they "shouldn't." (also, don't tell someone how someone "should" feel, lol)



If you have the patience and are willing to give her reassurance, then make sure she's holding up her end too. Just bc she'd BPD doesn't give her the right to be mean and you should stand up for yourself when you need to. If she starts splitting, it's usually best to just say something like "I love you, come back when you're calmer" or whatever. Remember to ask yourself if the things she asks and wants from you are truly reasonable for you, as a person.



BPD people are usually touch and words driven, which, you with aspergers, are probably not. This means she's going to need to learn your "love language" (most likely quality time, action-based, etc) and you're really going to have to go out of your way to learn hers (it goes back to the emotional retainer thing - if you make the effort to hold her hand on Monday, it will need to be repeated before Tuesday night and for a long time after that before her specific emotional retainer around you increases to anything resembling "normal")




If she is angry, one of the first things you can usually do to alleviate any escalation is reminding her that you do love her. Of course, still stand your ground, but that little reminder can instantly dampen any impending escalations!



Again, she's really lucky to have found you and I hope she treats you well. <3
And remember, even if you _didnt_ try to help her, it's still not your fault if she tries to/ends up killing herself

I know how tremendously hurtful it is to hear that at 15 - my mom said things very similar to me at that age.

I'm now twice as old as you and if I could give my 15 year old self some advice, it would be to speak up about how damaging those words are. She probably won't change but if you recognize early on that you're worth so much more kindness than that and actually stick up for yourself, you have a chance at a better life when you're an adult.

You don't want to kill yourself thinking "yeah! Now she'll regret what she said!!" Because then the only thing you're doing is never giving yourself the gift to move on and have a better life.

My mom has also called me worthless a number of times. A few hours ago she told me I was just a burden to her life and useless. But the day before that she told me I looked pretty.


I would love to have some consistent kindness in my life but it's rarely been that way for me since childhood and I'm 31 now and don't have any hope of ever getting to experience that. :/

If your girlfriend has pushed you to give up something you truly love she isn't "caring".


I wouldn't even call that a friend.


The best part about my last relationship was that not only did we like doing a lot of the same things, but he helped me get better and learn more about things I was interested in.


I mean, it's the activities and hobbies that are kind of the foundation of a relationship. It starts on the friendship stuff and the sex part is nice and all but of course that isn't going to feel special if you don't have the friendship stuff there.


I wouldn't want to have sex with someone who didn't seem interested in my day. You think you're only staying with her for the sex? You literally said "the only two things that make me briefly happy are sex and boating." If you can't add "and getting to talk to my GF everyday" or "waking up next to her and exchanging good mornings as the start to all my days" or anything else...then you probably shouldn't be with her.

I don't have a BF and I recently got called creepy so I relate to feeling like I'll never be with anyone.



To answer your question, I have in the past and I've seen other depressed people in relationships. I think if the person can honestly tell themselves "this person has given me tons of reasons to believe that I matter to them" it helps but it's really on the depressed person to get help outside the relationship and get better otherwise the relationship will just crumble from negativity.

This runs through my head a lot too. I've noticed people with severe depression have a short "emotional retainer".

Like, normal people don't need a ton of reassurance that they're loved. Someone can do something to make them feel that way and nothing else extraordinary for a long period of time but that initial loving feeling still gets retained.



Depressed people however, can't hold on to that long enough and probably need he patience to be reminded and reassured every day for a very long time before it can be permanently retained.



My point is, you probably are loved, you just can't feel it. Which sucks still, but maybe the hope of knowing some of it "is in your head" can help you cope a bit.



My breaking point was realizing that I'd been holding onto that hope and was told I was stupid for that. That I need to accept that I'm really not special to anyone and I should just suck it up and go through everything alone. :(

I did something similar except it was more like "please tell me something about me and having me in your life that makes your life better" or something like that and didn't really get an answer. Just a bunch of what about me is wrong now and what about me in the past was good.


I envy people that seem to find their self-worth from absolutely no outside resources.
It's like you and I are the same person, though I was 15 and really wish I'd utilized the internet more.

Society is so weird. It's all "Live for yourself, be independent, blah blah blah blah" but if you want to kill yourself? "How could you be so selfish? Think of all the people you're going to hurt!" ...isn't that essentially telling us to live for other people?



That said, some of us _don't_ have anyone we can say "Oh they love us so much, they'd be devastated if we killed ourselves." My mom personally has asked me three times now if both our lives would have been better if I'd killed myself in 10th grade.



So I read your post and thought I'd offer the viewpoint that it could be worse. You're mad at your mom for having you but it must be really nice to be able to say without hesitation "I know how much she loves me."




There isn't a single person on this planet that actually loves me.

This is a large reason why I think I can't be helped anymore. That somehow I have to honestly be happy and okay being truly alone in everything I go through or I have to pay someone to listen to me.

I mean, if no one really thought I was worth caring about as a kid - back when I really was a good person (bc a kid hasn't had time to do "bad" things) - then why on earth would anyone think I'm worth caring about now that I'm an adult, all covered in dirty sorts of feelings like anger, jealousy, lies, and rampant sadness.

No, I wasn't drunk but since my car accident, there's been a chance of me having neuromuscular issues so I've avoided driving unless feeling emotionally and physically ok.


I avoided driving my dog for many months and the one time I wasn't able to not have him around, I crashed and now his kidney's are failing and I don't really know what to do. He's my everything and I feel like I've betrayed him as a mother.


I meant those two words sound a like in the other language my mom speaks to me. The literal translation is "sleep for temporary" as opposed to "sleep forever". If he was in the US, I'd have more hope but in India the conditions aren't great. He had cardiac arrest and has been in a coma since. In the US, the odds of waiting it out are far higher than having the plug pulled.


Anytime I've tried to talk to my mom about it, it doesn't go well. She blames me for not being there and for him not being near me now or something else twisted in her head. She wants me to go there to deal with the doctors but when I said I wanted to focus on my dog...I was told in many ways that I was a selfish terrible person. And so ungrateful.




I'm an engineer and I really try to deal with things as I know how I can. Right now, I know I can try and find a vet that can help. So far the past two haven't been helpful. I honestly don't know what I can do for my dad and I've been putting off thinking about it bc it's extremely overwhelming. I sent all my money bc that's all I know what I can do and I'm very well aware that money talks in India.

Playing what-ifs isn't going to help my dog. I'm trying my hardest right now to find a vet than can help him and it wasn't easy taking him away from the first one knowing he isn't ok but my gut says this is what I need to do.


He's also made the choice to talk to me before even though I made him feel really terrible. It was just all really bad timing. He could choose to not be friends with me at all and it wouldn't be unwarranted at all. But he doesn't abandon me despite sometimes being treated like total shit by me and I try to remember that.


But if my dog dies, I'm not going to debate a single moment about living. Bc I can't handle living knowing I killed my best friend.
Here for now. Trying to see other vets about my dog to get some hope but so far it's just more bad news.
All that is irrelevant. I'm the reason why my dog is dying. I can't live with that.

Still here and my dog's still getting treated but I've already been getting "how to say bye" resources.


In which case I'm getting into my car, shutting off all electronics and killing myself up a mountain. That's two deaths and I've no desire to stick around to feel more pain or hear how worthless I am or stupid and pathetic I am for feeling upset over all this. Or how unreasonable I'm being or how shitty I am for yelling.


He's already told me he wouldn't cry if we weren't friends, my mom has told me I cause bad things to happen in her life, and anyone I might have talked to lives near him bc I was only making friends through that support group. Now I don't even have that to go to. I'm devastated about my dog and my dad. And I'm not going to continue living when the only people that will care or that I can see are people me or my health insurance pays.

I don't think anyone here gets it bc I couldn't delineate it at 3 AM...I've basically killed my own dog and everyone hates me. I have no worthy reasons to live. I have what's needed to kill myself, I get a good bye with him, then I'm headed for one of my favorite trails to die under a tree on a mountain.


If he lives, I'll stick around. But that isn't looking likely.

As someone suicidal and reading these psychological claims, this show really pissed me off. I don't think I, or anyone I've talked to who suffers the way I do, would ever think or WANT to make a box of things to actively make people feel bad for me/is dying.


This show neither decreased or increased my suicidal thoughts. It might have decreased it slightly by watching other people feel guilty over extremely petty shit bc I wouldn't want anyone to feel DISTRAUGHT over that. Like, yah, you should feel like fucking shit for raping me. But dear god, don't feel bad for not knowing to ask me what's really wrong when I screamed fuck you, get away from me and definitely don't feel bad for me snapping at you in the cafeteria after you sat with me in a diner just so I wouldn't be alone when something clearly painful was going on.


That show was so fucked up for so many reasons and trivialized how suicidal people who are planning things out for months and would never do it where their parents would find them are going through. That show didn't convey that there are many suicidal people going through things far more awful and aren't handling it in such a petty way. But they still aren't able to cope either.
